senses.sense_definition: A smaller format newspaper, typically featuring sensational stories, celebrity gossip, and many photographs.

examples.text: He bought a <w>tabloid</w> at the train station to read during his morning commute.
The scandal was plastered across the front page of every popular <w>tabloid</w>.

senses.sense_definition: A standard paper size measuring 11 by 17 inches, often used for printing larger documents.

examples.text: Please print the architectural drawings on <w>tabloid</w> paper so all details are visible.
The office printer ran out of <w>tabloid</w> sheets before the poster was finished.

senses.sense_definition: A small, compressed pill or tablet containing medicine, chemicals, or food substances.

examples.text: The old doctor carried a small vial of aspirin <w>tabloids</w> in his medical kit.
Dissolving one chemical <w>tabloid</w> into the water produced enough solution for the experiment.

senses.sense_definition: A compact or condensed version of something.

examples.text: The stage adaptation felt like a rushed <w>tabloid</w> of the monumental classic novel.
They presented a <w>tabloid</w> summary of the full financial report to the board.

senses.sense_definition: A small yacht designed for cruising.

examples.text: They spent the summer sailing along the coast in a vintage <w>tabloid</w> cruiser.
The tiny harbour was filled with several wooden <w>tabloids</w> moored for the winter.

senses.sense_definition: Characteristic of tabloid journalism; sensational, simplified, and focused on celebrity gossip or scandal.

examples.text: She refused to speak to reporters, tired of seeing her private life in <w>tabloid</w> headlines.
Critics dismissed the television program as cheap <w>tabloid</w> entertainment that lacked serious investigative value.

senses.sense_definition: Compressed, compact, or condensed in size or format.

examples.text: The book provided a <w>tabloid</w> overview of European history for busy tourists.
Modern audiences often prefer their news delivered in quick, <w>tabloid</w> snippets.

senses.sense_definition: To summarize or present something in a sensational, condensed manner typical of tabloid media.

examples.text: The media completely <w>tabloided</w> the tragic divorce to boost online viewership.
She accused the writer of deliberately <w>tabloiding</w> her words to make them sound scandalous.

senses.sense_definition: To redesign or convert a publication into a tabloid format.

examples.text: The publisher chose to <w>tabloid</w> the broadsheet to attract younger and busier readers.
Several local daily papers have been <w>tabloided</w> in an effort to reduce printing costs.
